feature: A click past the frame lets go of a zoomed recording
summary: With a recording pushed in, a click on the empty canvas outside the frame now lets go of it, like a click on empty canvas does for anything else. A click on the picture inside the frame still picks it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the sample recording with the timeline showing.

try.do: Click the recording, open Animate a property and pick Scale at 0:03.
Move the playhead to 0:05 and type 220 in Scale.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the empty canvas just left of the frame.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the picture inside the frame to pick the recording again.
Drag the picture to frame a different spot.

evaluate: Does a click past the frame let go of the recording the way you expect?
Does a click on the picture inside the frame always pick it back up?
Does dragging the picture after picking it again still frame the shot?
rough: No mock covers what a click past the frame does; this follows the frame ring the walkthrough draws, so the click and the ring now agree.
A recording at its own size slid partly off the canvas still picks from the part hanging off, where its outline is drawn. Only a pushed-in recording is cut off at the frame.
